subject.title: RFC: Distributed Agent Runtime — separate control plane from agent compute

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this Gateway/control-plane and per-agent runtime split as a core architecture track, and if so what is the first supported milestone?
rationale: The remaining work requires choosing public protocol, config, security, lifecycle, and migration boundaries; automation cannot safely pick those product and security contracts.

options.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
options.body: Keep #42026 as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

options.title: Narrow To Execution Placement
options.body: Treat #82017 and #84758 as the current scope and defer the broader Gateway/control-plane split until the smaller backend contract is settled.

options.title: Defer Core Architecture Change
options.body: Continue supporting multi-gateway/operator workarounds and plugin or harness improvements without committing to a distributed runtime boundary now.

recommendation.title: Approve Phased Runtime Split
recommendation.body: Keep #42026 as the canonical RFC and sponsor a first milestone that defines protocol, trust model, and local-split lifecycle before container or Kubernetes runners.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest current-main history signal across Gateway/agent runtime docs, CLI lifecycle, embedded harness, and the worker-runtime experiment connected to the RFC.
